changelog: v344: a birthday is a birth, and anyone's age is measured from their own birth. WHERE IT WAS SEEN: the owner reviewed staging on 2026-09-24. He had filed his mother's birthday ten days earlier as a manual source — `sources/manual/2026-09-14-desiree-birthday-1955-06-19.md`, "Desiree Taylor (Dave's mom, also called Desi) — birthday June 19, 1955." — and the classifier read it perfectly: `claim:da4f59afb2d774e0b9ebef87` (`classifier-claims/rule:5`), `claim_type: date`, 1955-06-19 certain/stated, `event_mention: "Desiree Taylor's birthday"`, `subject_mention: "Desiree Taylor (Desi)"`, `subject_ref: null`. Three things then went wrong at once on `node:8a3a570270bef180b1bb9eb7`. Its `event_kind` was `moment` — a claim extractor can say WHEN and cannot say what KIND of event a birthday is — so `births_by_subject`, which reads birth-kinded nodes, never saw it. Its subject resolved to nobody: the person roster's thirteen rows held a COLLECTIVE `parents` ("Mom and Dad (parents)") and no mother, so "Desiree Taylor", "Desi", "Mom" and "mother" answered to no one at all. And it published `axis_membership: owner / lived` — drawn on the owner's own axis as something he lived, twenty-six years before his 1981-07-11 birth — because `_owner_relevance`'s zero-candidate fallback reads a name the roster cannot place as the ordinary shape of the owner's own life. WHAT HE SAW were the consequences, as cards. "When did Mom married dad at 21 happen?" (`claim:34c92ccbf218e122a181ca5f`, an `age` claim of 21 with `subject_mention: "mother"`, from answers/K14.md) stayed `age_without_birth_anchor` although her birthday was in the same vault. And "When did Harvey explains rule about cussing happen?" (`claim:73bf36cabc03f2c4fd3b397e`, age 4, `subject_mention: "Harvey"`, from a source captured 2026-08-29 that literally says "Harvey boy is four years old") could not anchor either, because Harvey's own merged birth node (`node:f617262f723b943266375d93`, 2021-10-11, eleven tellings folded by the binder's `R2b`) came out of the v340 fold labelled "your birth" with the OWNER as its subject — two of those tellings carry `subject_mention: "self"` because the owner is the subject of the TURNING POINT and the birth is only what turned it — and so minted the card "Two dates are claimed for your birth — 11 October 2021 and 2020. Which is right?" about a child's birthday. THE RULES, one definition each, all of them extensions of v339–v342 rather than exceptions to them. (1) A DATED BIRTHDAY IS A BIRTH (`temporal_timeline.A_DATED_BIRTHDAY_IS_A_BIRTH`, applied by `reads_as_a_birth`/`_read_event_kind`): a `date` claim whose event mention names a person's birth, at day, month or year grain, with a named non-owner subject, IS that person's `birth`. The vocabulary is `landmark_projection.BIRTH_EVENT_NOUNS` with the predicate `birth_event_subject` — a SUBSET of v341's one birth vocabulary, asked forwards ("whose birth is this?") instead of backwards ("does this name nobody?"), compared whole and never as a substring, so "Mary Born" and "Bornstein" are still names and "Harvey's birthday party" is still a party. It is a READING over the substrate, taken where the fold decides what a group is, so a vault that already holds the claim heals on its next redraw and the receipt still says exactly what the extractor said; and the owner's own birth is excluded by construction (an owner `subject_ref`, an owner-only mention and a bare birth domain word all refuse), so v339/v340 keep governing it alone. (2) THE PERSON EXISTS (`roster_relations.A_RELATIONSHIP_PHRASE_INTRODUCES_A_PERSON`): a named subject the roster has never heard of, introduced in its own source by a relationship phrase the owner used — "Dave's mom", "my mother", "(wife)", "(brother)", "my mother-in-law Ruth" — gets a roster row with that `relationship`, derived from `identity_resolution.RELATIONSHIP_MENTION_WORDS` crossed with `focus_candidate.FOCUS_RELATIONSHIPS` so mother/father land in the `parent` tier of `axis_membership`'s immediate-family set and an in-law lands in `other`. The possessive must be the OWNER'S: "Katie's mom" is not his mother. Aliases are the mention as written, any nickname it carries ("Desi") and the relationship spellings the phrase licenses, by SET EQUALITY over the satisfaction sets so "mom" brings "mother" and never "dad" — and an alias more than one introduced person claims is dropped from EVERY row before anything is written, which is the v335 shared-alias rule stated over the whole batch instead of decided by file order. The write is `entity_roster.ensure_introduced_relatives`, one seat, through `entity_verdict.apply_verdict(..., ensure=True)` — the `source: "landmark:family"` door the `james` and `anthon-james-taylor` rows already came through — reached by `entity-roster --ensure-introduced [--dry-run]`: deterministic, no AI, one atomic per-row write, additive, never a rewrite of the file and never a hand-edit. (3) ANYONE'S AGE ANCHORS ON THEIR OWN BIRTH (`AN_AGE_IS_MEASURED_FROM_ITS_OWN_SUBJECT`): `_births_by_subject` reads `BIRTH_ANCHOR_TIERS` in order — a birth-kinded node whose resolved subject is that person, else the roster row's `born`, else a `family`/`children` landmark entry's own date, those two being the domains whose ladder DECLARES `date_semantics: ["birth"]` (`landmark_projection.BIRTH_DATE_SEMANTICS_DOMAINS`, pinned by a parity test against `questions.yaml` so a ladder that changes its semantics fails the build rather than teaching the arithmetic to read a wedding as a birthday). The first tier that answers for a person answers for every key that person goes by, so a lower tier can add a birth nobody has drawn and can never contradict one already on the page; a key several roster people bear is never one of those keys, because four people on the owner's roster bear the token *James* and a bare "James" must go on naming none of them. Tier one now reads its BEST-SUPPORTED value rather than refusing a contested birth, which is exactly how the owner's own anchor has always been read: :14 refused here and fell through, so Harvey's contradicted birth handed the age arithmetic the LOSING 2020 reading off his roster row, silently, while the card that would settle it stayed open. `_record_for_age_claim` and `chronology.from_age_band` are untouched and still subject-agnostic — they take a birth and a band and do arithmetic — so the only thing that changed is WHICH birth a group is handed, and `age_without_birth_anchor` is now reported exactly when none of the three exists. (4) THE MERGED BIRTH CARRIES THE CHILD'S SUBJECT (`A_BIRTH_BELONGS_TO_THE_PERSON_BORN`, which is v339's `OWNER_BIRTH_IS_ABOUT_NOBODY_ELSE` read forwards): a birth group naming exactly one non-owner person — one `subject_ref`, identity landed — is that person's birth whatever else it mentions, because a birth has one subject and the owner's `self` mentions on such a group are the turning point he lived. `_group_claims` applies it after every node id is minted, so no node moves; `_is_owner_subject` reads the same one definition, so the title, the contradiction card, the age anchor and the origin floor cannot answer the question four ways. Two named people on one birth group decide nothing and are left to v340's `owner_birth_anchor_ambiguous`. v340's refusal semantics are intact and asserted. (5) PRE-BIRTH IS NEVER LIVED: rule 4 of the owner's axis ruling moved ABOVE the evidence relations and above an unidentified subject in `axis_membership`, so a node wholly before his birth is `pre_birth` whoever it turns out to be about; and `_owner_relevance`'s zero-candidate fallback no longer claims a wholly pre-birth moment as his own life. v334's exception is kept exactly: an occurrence whose subject IS the owner stays `owner`/`lived` before his birth, because that is a contradiction Mirror owns and hiding it off the axis would delete the question. `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` takes `timeline-rules:15` — `:13` and `:14` went to v343 and v345, which both landed while this branch was open: a different node set, a different placement set and a different work-item set for claims nobody edited. RE-RUN, after the rebase onto v343, on a scratch clone of the owner's vault (`2b15c1c0`) — publish with v343 bytes, overlay these, `entity-roster --ensure-introduced`, publish. Generation 152 → 153. Four people introduced and filed: his mother (`desiree-taylor`, parent, born 1955-06-19, aliases Desi/mom/my mom/mother/my mother), his wife (`katie-taylor`, spouse, born 1987-05-15, aliases wife/my wife) and his father under BOTH spellings the vault holds (`james-taylor` and `james-edwin-taylor-sr`, parent), with "dad"/"father" bound to neither of the two because the vault names him twice. 0 placements lost, 0 dated moments moved, 3 new age placements — "Mom married dad at 21" 1976-06-19/1977-06-18, which OVERLAPS the parents' wedding landmark of 1976-06-25 in `state/landmarks.json` and is the corroboration the owner will see; "Harvey explains rule about cussing" and "Harvey's late talking start" 2025-10-11/2026-10-10, the first of which contains the source's own capture date of 2026-08-29. Nodes 1188 → 1189, placed 1155 → 1158, age-basis placements 42 → 45, `age_without_birth_anchor` 16 → 13, open cards 40 → 38 (`precision_gap` 32 → 30, `contradiction` 7 → 7, `identity_uncertain` 1 → 1). `node:8a3a570270bef180b1bb9eb7` is now "Desiree Taylor's birth", birth-kinded, subject `person/desiree-taylor`, `axis_membership: none / pre_birth` — family history on her page, which is ruling 4's own answer and the reason it is not `family`: `family` MEANS drawn on his axis. `node:f617262f723b943266375d93` is now "Harvey's birth" with subject `person/harvey`, and its card reads "Two dates are claimed for Harvey's birth — 11 October 2021 and 2020." The owner's own anchor is still the single 1981-07-11 and his five age frames are byte-identical. Three grandparents' pasted birthdays (1929-09-30, 1930-10-17, 1932-09-16) became birth-kinded too and read `pre_birth`; 43 nodes moved off `owner`/`lived` — 32 to `family`/`immediate_family_in_lifetime` because his mother, father and wife now resolve, and 11 to `pre_birth` because a nameless pre-birth scene was never his. KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: adding a roster row re-keys a node whose subject newly resolves and whose claims carry no `event_ref` of their own — one such node appeared on the rig, an undated second "Mom babysat Kodi and Acey Nixon" — because a node id is derived from its subject and v342's `node_aliases` covers a BINDER re-key, not an identity one. That is the binder's seam, not the fold's. GUARDS: `tests/test_v344_a_birthday_is_a_birth.py` (64 tests) — the vocabulary as a unit with v341's own refusals still refusing and the containment in `BIRTH_DOMAIN_WORDS` pinned; the ladder parity test; `reads_as_a_birth` against every owner spelling, every recorded kind it may not re-decide, a range it must refuse and all three grains it accepts; the introduction rule against every shape the owner's vault writes and against "Katie's mom", a mention with no name, and an in-law; the writer seat on a synthetic vault (row, dry run, convergence, and an alias an existing row already answers to being left alone); the three tiers in order with the birth node outranking the roster and the landmark, a contested birth still anchoring, a shared name token anchoring nobody and two birth groups for one person anchoring nothing; the merged group resolving to the child with the card naming him and the owner's anchor still single; the axis ordering exhaustively over every scope/relation/tier/pre-birth combination with v334's exception intact; and the owner's whole review as one fold. `tests/test_eras_e2.py` gains the pre-birth half of its own negative control and moves that control's date inside the owner's life. Docs: ADR 0037 gains its v344 amendment, the eras handbook its rule-version row. REBASED twice before merge, onto v343 (card quality gate) and then onto v345 (a telling of a landmark folds onto it), both of which landed while this branch was open and both of which touch this fold. v343's empty-claim gate runs before this release's kind reading in `_group_claims`; v345's `birth_for_claim` — "an age is the age of the person the CLAIM is about" — now reads THIS release's three-tier `births_by_subject` rather than the single tier it was written against, which is the two rules composing rather than colliding; and tier three asks v345's `landmark_projection.entry_date_event_kind` instead of the ladder's declaration alone, so the owner's one `family` entry — his PARENTS at 1976-06-25, a wedding, and a couple is never born — anchors nobody's age. Version 344 and 345, and `timeline-rules:13` and `:14`, were taken by those releases; this ships as 346 on `:15`. The whole suite was re-run on each rebase.
